title: Neighbors and community
theme: Borrowing, a noise feud, carrying things for each other, a block gathering, the stall keeper who knows everyone.

storylets.title: Can I borrow your ladder
storylets.note: A neighbor borrows a thing. Chain: nbr.tool-returned, or it quietly stays borrowed.

A.desc: an adult at a neighbor's door

b1: {A} knocks at a door two along from {A.his} own and stands back.
{A} raps on the door and waits with hands behind {A.his} back.
{A} knocks lightly, three taps.
b2: The door opens. {B.desc} hands {A} a coil of rope and a short ladder.
{B.desc} holds out a toolbox. {A} takes the handle.
{B.desc} passes {A} a power drill, cord wrapped around it.
b3: {A} carries it off down the block, the ladder knocking the rail.
{A} hauls the load back to {A.his} own door, thanking the air.
{A} walks away with the rope looped over a shoulder.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Take it, neighbor. Just bring it back before the weekend."
Overheard: {A} says: "What would I do without a {B.rel} like you?"
Overheard: {A} says: "You saved me again. Come by for dumplings on Sunday."

b1: {A} hauls a ladder along the block, a paper bag swinging from one rung.
{A} comes down the row carrying a drill in both hands.
{A} walks up with the toolbox held at arm's length.
b2: {A} hands the tool back. {B.desc} checks the cord twice.
{A} hands over a bag of sweets and the tool.
{A} holds out the loan with a small bow. {B.desc} laughs.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} chat on the step, then {B.desc} points down the block.
{B.desc} says something that makes {A} grin. A short wave.
The two trade a few words over a shared fence.

storylets.title: The knock after midnight
storylets.note: A noise complaint at a door. Chain: nbr.peace-offering, or a feud that never lands.

A.desc: an adult at a neighbor's door

b1: {A} bangs on a neighbor's door, jaw tight.
{A} knocks hard and keeps knocking.
{A} pounds on the door, a hand on the frame.
b2: The door opens. {B.desc} and {A} argue across the threshold.
{B.desc} snaps at {A} and {A} snaps right back. Voices carry.
{A} jabs a finger toward the ceiling. {B.desc} folds both arms.
b3: {A} leaves, stamping down the step.
{A} turns on a heel and goes off into the night.
{A} walks away shaking {A.his} head.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "Every night, the same drum! Some of us work in the morning!"
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Then knock like a person, not a hammer."

storylets.title: A plate on the step
storylets.note: Pays off the noise knock. A plate, a note, a nod.

A.desc: an adult at a neighbor's door

b1: {A} climbs the step carrying a covered plate.
{A} comes to a neighbor's door with a steaming dish in both hands.
{A} arrives with a plate under a cloth, shoulders stiff.
b2: The door slides open. {A} holds out the plate. {B.desc} takes it.
{A} hands the plate over with a few mumbled words.
{A} passes the dish across. {B.desc} peers under the cloth.
b3: {B.desc} nods slowly and says a few words. {A} lets out a breath.
{A} and {B.desc} talk. A hand goes out, a hand is shaken.
They speak low. The door stays open a while after.

storylets.title: A hand with the shopping
storylets.note: A younger neighbor carries bags for an older one.

b1: {B.desc} crosses the block slowly, a bag in each hand and a third on the arm.
{B.desc} climbs the sidewalk slope, stopping every few steps.
{B.desc} makes a slow way home, shopping dragging.
b2: {A} catches up and takes two of the bags without a word.
{A} jogs over, lifts the heaviest bag, and falls into step.
{A} relieves {B.desc} of the load and walks alongside.
b3: Both go in at the same door. The door slides shut on a thank-you.
{A} follows {B.desc} up and in with the bags.
{B.desc} unlocks, and {A} goes in with the shopping.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Thank you. You are a good {A.rel}."
Overheard: {A} says: "Anytime. That's what a {A.rel} is for."
Overheard: {A} says: "Anytime. Call down the hall, I will hear."

storylets.title: Everybody on the stoop
storylets.note: A small block gathering. A good place for names and relations to leak out.

b1: {A}, {B.desc} and {C.desc} gather at the edge of the square with folding stools.
A little knot of neighbors forms around {A}, {B.desc} and {C.desc}.
{A} arrives with a pot; {B.desc} and {C.desc} are already unfolding stools.
b2: Bowls go round the circle. {C.desc} refuses seconds three times, then accepts.
{A} ladles a stew into mismatched bowls and hands them out.
{B.desc} breaks a flatbread and passes the pieces around.
b3: The circle talks over itself. {A} laughs at something {B.desc} says.
{C.desc} tells a long story. {B.desc} corrects the details.
Voices overlap. {A} points toward the roofs and the others turn.

log: Overheard: {C.desc} says: "{B.first}, you tell it, you were there."
Overheard: {A} calls: "{B.first}! Bring the salt."

storylets.title: The usual, by name
storylets.note: A shopkeeper who knows the regulars. The best way for a first name to leak out, verified by a loyalty card.

b1: {A} steps up to the counter without looking at the board.
{A} reaches the stall and holds up two fingers.
{A} gets to the front and says nothing. The keeper nods.
{A} arrives at the counter and puts coins down.
b2: {B.desc} serves {A}'s order before it is spoken.
{B.desc} already has the cup out. {A} grins.
{B.desc} slides the usual across the counter.
{B.desc} serves {A} and adds a small extra.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} trade three sentences about the weather and the price of noodles.
{B.desc} asks after something; {A} waves a hand and answers.
They chat over the steam for a minute.
{B.desc} laughs at what {A} says and wipes the counter.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "The usual, {A.first}? Sit, I'll bring it."
Overheard: {B.desc} calls: "{A.first}! Your stool's open."
The keeper starts {A}'s order before {A.he} says a word.
The keeper has a cup out for {A} before {A.he} reaches the counter.

storylets.title: This one is for next door

b1: A drone lowers a small parcel at {A}'s door and rises.
{A} takes a parcel from a drone and squints at the label.
A delivery drone leaves a package at the wrong step. {A} lifts it.
b2: {A} walks to the next door and knocks.
{A} raps on the neighbor's door with the parcel under one arm.
{A} knocks once and waits.
b3: The door slides open. {A} hands the parcel to {B.desc} and shrugs.
{A} holds out the parcel. {B.desc} takes it and bows.
{A} hands over the package and points at the drone's path.

log: The label reads {B.full}, one door along.
The parcel is addressed to {B.full}.

storylets.title: Something hot for the new tenant
storylets.note: A neighbor brings food to someone who just moved in. Uses the game's own new-neighbor flag.

A.desc: an adult with a covered dish

b1: {A} carries a covered dish across the landing.
{A} comes down the row with a steaming pot held in a towel.
{A} walks to the newest door with a plate and a spoon.
b2: {A} knocks and waits, straightening a collar.
{A} raps on the door and stands back with the dish held forward.
{A} knocks twice. A voice answers faintly.
b3: The door opens. {A} hands the dish to {B.desc} and says a few words.
{A} hands over the dish. {B.desc} bows and takes it with both hands.
{A} passes the pot across the threshold.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "You are the first one to knock. Thank you, neighbor."
Overheard: {A} says: "Welcome. I'm your {A.rel}, just across the hall."
Overheard: {A} says: "Welcome to the block. I live just across, if you need anything."

storylets.title: The saucer on the curb
storylets.note: A neighbor feeds a stray; another passes and speaks.

b1: {A} sets a saucer on the curb and crouches while a thin cat approaches.
{A} scatters scraps by a drain. A stray eats, flinching at every sound.
{A} crouches by the wall and puts out a dish.
b2: {B.desc} comes along the sidewalk with a bag and slows down.
{B.desc} walks up the block and stops to look.
{B.desc} passes the corner, then turns back.
b3: {B.desc} says something about the cat. {A} shrugs and answers.
{A} and {B.desc} talk across the saucer. {B.desc} laughs.
{B.desc} bends down too, and the two argue softly over names.

log: {A} fills a saucer here for the strays: {seen} mornings on the feed.
{A} fills the saucer. The cat comes to it.

storylets.title: Two doors, one conversation
storylets.note: Neighbors trade talk across a landing. Conversations carry names and news.

A.desc: an adult chatting at a door

b1: {A} leans on {A.his} doorframe while {B.desc} stops at the next step.
{B.desc} halts at {A}'s door, bag on one hip.
{A} stands in the doorway as {B.desc} hovers by the rail.
{A} and {B.desc} meet at the landing.
b2: They talk about the noise from the lift and the price of broth.
{A} points down the block and {B.desc} shakes a head.
{B.desc} says something low and {A} laughs.
The two of them gossip for ten minutes, hands moving.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "They are putting a new stall on the corner. Rent is going up, mark me."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "I heard the lift will be closed all of Thursday."
